judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-outs use highly contestable terms — "restitution, disgorgement, or payment of similar sums," "depreciation (or failure to appreciate) in value of any investment product ... due to market fluctuation unrelated to any Wrongful Act," and the catch-all "any matters which are uninsurable under the law" — each of which invites competing readings of what a covered Loss is. The general/specific structure (an enumerated list closed by an open-ended (7) and (8)) is exactly the kind of ejusdem generis problem courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fiduciary Liability Endorsement deletes and replaces this Loss definition with a differently worded list (omitting the investment-depreciation and prior-contract carve-outs), so which definition governs a given Claim must be worked out across the instrument. Item (5)'s prior-contract carve-out also sits awkwardly with the Contract Exclusions in Sections VI(B) and the endorsements, giving a real, if resolvable, integration question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "By, on behalf of, or at the behest of the Company ... in any capacity" is the classic ambiguity in D&O policies — whether a receiver or successor suing in the company's name is within it — and the carve-outs' "brought and maintained ... totally without the solicitation, assistance, participation, or intervention of any other Insured" adds a vague boundary. Both phrases are precisely the sort of terms a court is asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion overlaps and partially duplicates the Collusion Exclusion in Section V(C) and is deleted and replaced with a four-part version by the Fiduciary Liability Endorsement, so its reach differs by insuring agreement. The interaction with Insuring Agreement (B)'s indemnification coverage (which presupposes company-funded claims) is a further point of tension worth checking.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for the Company's own securities is what preserves the Securities Liability grant, but limb (2)'s exclusion of advice about offerings of securities cuts back toward it; harmonising the two is a real exercise.
